description: Write a BigQuery MERGE statement that applies a staging batch of product changes to the target dimension table. Rules: (1) the staging batch may contain several rows per product_id; only the row with the latest updated_at (ties: highest staging_seq) is applied; (2) if the winning staging row has is_deleted = TRUE, delete the product from the target (do nothing if absent); (3) if the product exists in the target, update it only when staging updated_at is strictly newer than the target's updated_at; (4) if the product does not exist and is not deleted, insert it. The expected output is the full content of products_target after the MERGE. Output columns: product_id (INT64), price (FLOAT64), updated_at (TIMESTAMP).

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last applied change

product_id.description: Business key; not unique in staging

price.description: New price; NULL on delete rows

is_deleted.description: TRUE when the product was removed at source

edge_cases: Two staging rows for product 1: only the newest is applied
Stale staging row for product 3 (older than target) must not overwrite the target
Delete for product 2 removes the row; a delete for a product absent from the target must not insert anything
Re-running the same MERGE must leave the target unchanged (idempotent)
common_failure_modes: FM4: MERGE with a non-deduplicated source fails in BigQuery with 'UPDATE/MERGE must match at most one source row for each target row'
FM3: WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT without excluding is_deleted rows inserts tombstones as products with NULL price
FM7: No updated_at guard in WHEN MATCHED lets late-arriving stale data overwrite newer values
